evidence: With the window fitted to the coverage (window_support, on by default), the backend keeps at most support_tol = 1e-3 of the window's weight on unmeasured space: auto keeps the separable window only under it (src/nebula3d/analysis/delta_pdf.py:1146), else shrinks an ellipsoid until it holds (:1218; support_tol :397). qmax_coverage judged that weight against the same 1e-3 (web/src/llm/metrics/coverage.ts:8, web/src/llm/verdicts/rules.ts:436), so its "clean" held by construction, as did a reach taken from the taper: the dev cut read 8.97e-4 on 81³ and 9.82e-4 on 161³. Its note that "only the window's taper keeps the transform on the counts" was said where no taper is fitted too, the support off or a separable window (rules.ts:461). band_check called a band with no Qmin below the counts' lower edge on counts that begin at the origin (web/src/llm/tools/defs/qmax_coverage.ts:160), though the run starts such a band at 0 (web/src/state/pipelineStore.ts:401).
proposed_fix: With the window fitted (the support on, an auto or ellipsoid window, its support seeing where the counts end), the verdict opens "fitted to the coverage", says the weight the ΔPDF records, or the taper's reach without one, is the backend's own target, not a check (reason window fitted), and judges where the counts end (batch 1's sentence and data problem) and a band that is set: past the counts' edges it needs attention ("too far: Qmax past the counts' upper edge …", reason band past counts), the user's rule (reduction-qc step 3); inside them it passes. A weight recorded past the limit is judged as before. Without the fit the weight or the reach is judged as before, and the note no longer says a taper keeps the transform on the counts. A band with no Qmin is taken from 0, as the run takes it.
